sentences.en: According to a leading business consultancy, 3–14% of the global workforce will need to switch to a different occupation within the next 10–15 years, and all workers will need to adapt as their occupations evolve alongside increasingly capable machines.
sentences.zh: 据一家知名商业咨询机构预测，未来10至15年，全球3%至14%的劳动者将需要转行；随着职业和能力日益强大的机器一道演变，所有劳动者都需要适应。

sentences.en: Automation – or ‘embodied artificial intelligence’ (AI) – is one aspect of the disruptive effects of technology on the labour market.
sentences.zh: 自动化，也称“具身人工智能”（AI），是技术给劳动力市场带来颠覆性影响的一个方面。

sentences.en: ‘Disembodied AI’, like the algorithms running in our smartphones, is another.
sentences.zh: “非具身人工智能”则是另一个方面，比如智能手机里运行的算法。

sentences.en: Dr Stella Pachidi from Cambridge Judge Business School believes that some of the most fundamental changes are happening as a result of the ‘algorithmication’ of jobs that are dependent on data rather than on production – the so-called knowledge economy.
sentences.zh: 剑桥大学贾奇商学院的斯特拉·帕基迪博士认为，一些最根本的变化正在发生，原因在于一些工作正在“算法化”。这些工作依托的是数据而非生产活动，也就是所谓的知识经济。

sentences.en: Algorithms are capable of learning from data to undertake tasks that previously needed human judgement, such as reading legal contracts, analysing medical scans and gathering market intelligence.
sentences.zh: 算法能从数据中学习，从而承担过去需要人类判断的任务，例如阅读法律合同、分析医学扫描影像以及收集市场情报。

sentences.en: ‘In many cases, they can outperform humans,’ says Pachidi.
sentences.zh: “很多时候，算法的表现能超过人类，”帕基迪说。

sentences.en: ‘Organisations are attracted to using algorithms because they want to make choices based on what they consider is “perfect information”, as well as to reduce costs and enhance productivity.’
sentences.zh: “各类组织之所以愿意使用算法，是因为它们既希望依据自己眼中的‘完备信息’来做选择，也希望降低成本、提高生产率。”

sentences.en: ‘But these enhancements are not without consequences,’ says Pachidi.
sentences.zh: “不过，这些改进也会带来后果，”帕基迪说。

sentences.en: ‘If routine cognitive tasks are taken over by AI, how do professions develop their future experts?’ she asks.
sentences.zh: “如果常规的认知任务交给人工智能，各行各业又该怎样培养未来的专家呢？”她问道。

sentences.en: ‘One way of learning about a job is “legitimate peripheral participation” – a novice stands next to experts and learns by observation.
sentences.zh: “学习一项工作的方式之一叫作‘合法的边缘性参与’：新手待在专家身边，通过观察来学习。

sentences.en: If this isn’t happening, then you need to find new ways to learn.’
sentences.zh: 如果少了这个过程，就需要另找学习途径。”

sentences.en: Another issue is the extent to which the technology influences or even controls the workforce.
sentences.zh: 另一个问题是，这项技术在多大程度上影响、甚至控制劳动者。

sentences.en: For over two years, Pachidi monitored a telecommunications company.
sentences.zh: 帕基迪对一家电信公司进行了两年多的跟踪观察。

sentences.en: ‘The way telecoms salespeople work is through personal and frequent contact with clients, using the benefit of experience to assess a situation and reach a decision.
sentences.zh: “电信销售人员的工作方式，是亲自与客户保持频繁联系，凭借经验判断情况并作出决定。

sentences.en: However, the company had started using a[n] ... algorithm that defined when account managers should contact certain customers about which kinds of campaigns and what to offer them.’
sentences.zh: 然而，该公司已开始使用一种……算法，由它来规定客户经理应在何时联系哪些客户，谈哪些营销活动，以及向客户提供什么。”

sentences.en: The algorithm – usually built by external designers – often becomes the keeper of knowledge, she explains.
sentences.zh: 她解释说，算法通常由外部设计人员构建，却常常成了掌管知识的一方。

sentences.en: In cases like this, Pachidi believes, a short-sighted view begins to creep into working practices whereby workers learn through the ‘algorithm’s eyes’ and become dependent on its instructions.
sentences.zh: 帕基迪认为，遇到这种情况，一种短视的观念就会悄然渗入工作方式：人们开始透过“算法的眼睛”来学习，并逐渐依赖它的指令。

sentences.en: Alternative explorations – where experimentation and human instinct lead to progress and new ideas – are effectively discouraged.
sentences.zh: 其他探索途径，即让试验和人的直觉带来进展、新想法的途径，实际上受到了抑制。

sentences.en: Pachidi and colleagues even observed people developing strategies to make the algorithm work to their own advantage.
sentences.zh: 帕基迪和同事甚至观察到，有人会想办法让算法为自己谋利。

sentences.en: ‘We are seeing cases where workers feed the algorithm with false data to reach their targets,’ she reports.
sentences.zh: “我们看到，有些员工为了达成指标，给算法输入虚假数据，”她报告说。

sentences.en: It’s scenarios like these that many researchers are working to avoid.
sentences.zh: 许多研究人员正致力于避免的，正是这类情形。

sentences.en: Their objective is to make AI technologies more trustworthy and transparent, so that organisations and individuals understand how AI decisions are made.
sentences.zh: 他们的目标是让人工智能技术更值得信赖、更透明，以便组织和个人能了解人工智能是怎样作出决策的。

sentences.en: In the meantime, says Pachidi, ‘We need to make sure we fully understand the dilemmas that this new world raises regarding expertise, occupational boundaries and control.’
sentences.zh: 与此同时，帕基迪说：“我们需要确保自己充分理解这个新世界在专业知识、职业界限和控制权方面带来的种种难题。”

sentences.en: Economist Professor Hamish Low believes that the future of work will involve major transitions across the whole life course for everyone: ‘The traditional trajectory of full-time education followed by full-time work followed by a pensioned retirement is a thing of the past,’ says Low.
sentences.zh: 经济学家哈米什·洛教授认为，在未来的工作世界中，每个人的一生都会经历重大转变。“先接受全日制教育，再全职工作，然后退休领取养老金，这条传统的人生轨迹已经成为过去，”洛说。

sentences.en: Instead, he envisages a multistage employment life: one where retraining happens across the life course, and where multiple jobs and no job happen by choice at different stages.
sentences.zh: 相比之下，他设想人们的职业生涯会分为多个阶段：一生中都可以接受再培训，也可以在不同阶段主动选择身兼数职或暂不工作。

sentences.en: On the subject of job losses, Low believes the predictions are founded on a fallacy: ‘It assumes that the number of jobs is fixed.
sentences.zh: 谈到工作岗位流失，洛认为有关预测建立在一个错误前提上：“它假定岗位总数是固定的。

sentences.en: If in 30 years, half of 100 jobs are being carried out by robots, that doesn’t mean we are left with just 50 jobs for humans.
sentences.zh: 如果30年后，100份工作中有一半由机器人做，也不能由此断定只剩50份工作留给人类。

sentences.en: The number of jobs will increase: we would expect there to be 150 jobs.’
sentences.zh: 岗位数量会增长：我们预计到时会有150个岗位。”

sentences.en: Dr Ewan McGaughey, at Cambridge’s Centre for Business Research and King’s College London, agrees that ‘apocalyptic’ views about the future of work are misguided.
sentences.zh: 剑桥大学商业研究中心和伦敦国王学院的尤恩·麦高伊博士也认为，把工作的未来看成“末日将临”，是受了误导。

sentences.en: ‘It’s the laws that restrict the supply of capital to the job market, not the advent of new technologies that causes unemployment.’
sentences.zh: “造成失业的是限制资本流入就业市场的法律，并非新技术的出现。”

sentences.en: His recently published research answers the question of whether automation, AI and robotics will mean a ‘jobless future’ by looking at the causes of unemployment.
sentences.zh: 他最近发表的研究从失业的成因着眼，回答了这样一个问题：自动化、人工智能和机器人技术是否意味着“无工可做的未来”？

sentences.en: ‘History is clear that change can mean redundancies.
sentences.zh: “历史清楚地表明，变革可能意味着裁员。

sentences.en: But social policies can tackle this through retraining and redeployment.’
sentences.zh: 但社会政策可以通过再培训和重新调配岗位来应对这个问题。”

sentences.en: He adds: ‘If there is going to be change to jobs as a result of AI and robotics then I’d like to see governments seizing the opportunity to improve policy to enforce good job security.
sentences.zh: 他补充说：“如果人工智能和机器人技术将使工作岗位发生变化，那么我希望看到各国政府抓住机会改进政策，切实保障就业稳定。

sentences.en: We can “reprogramme” the law to prepare for a fairer future of work and leisure.’
sentences.zh: 我们可以给法律‘重新编程’，为一个工作与休闲都更加公平的未来做好准备。”

sentences.en: McGaughey’s findings are a call to arms to leaders of organisations, governments and banks to pre-empt the coming changes with bold new policies that guarantee full employment, fair incomes and a thriving economic democracy.
sentences.zh: 麦高伊的研究结果向各组织、政府和银行的领导者发出了行动号召，呼吁他们用大胆的新政策为即将到来的变化预作准备，以保障充分就业、公平的收入和蓬勃发展的经济民主。

sentences.en: ‘The promises of these new technologies are astounding.
sentences.zh: “这些新技术的前景令人惊叹。

sentences.en: They deliver humankind the capacity to live in a way that nobody could have once imagined,’ he adds.
sentences.zh: 它们让人类有能力以过去谁也想象不到的方式生活，”他补充说。

sentences.en: ‘Just as the industrial revolution brought people past subsistence agriculture, and the corporate revolution enabled mass production, a third revolution has been pronounced.
sentences.zh: “正如工业革命让人们走出了仅能维持生计的农业，企业革命使大规模生产成为可能，如今第三场革命也已宣告到来。

sentences.en: But it will not only be one of technology.
sentences.zh: 但它将不只是一场技术革命。

sentences.en: The next revolution will be social.’
sentences.zh: 下一场革命将是一场社会革命。”
